newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on rates cut, zero-coupon.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on rates cut, zero-coupon.

text.p: The Thai bourse, which fell to its lowest level this year on Monday, was seen rising on Tuesday on local bank rates cuts and expectation the cabinet would approve the issue of zero-coupon bonds, brokers said.

"The market sentiment is expected to improve today after major banks cut their interest rates from today. Plans by the cabinet to approve zero-coupon bonds during its meeting today will also help boost the sentiment," said Supavat Saicheua of KrungThai Thanakit.
The composite SET index dropped 11.52 points to 672.48 on 2.5 billion baht turnover on Monday.
Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and Krung Thai Bank Plc announced a 25 basis point cut in their minimum lending rates, effective today.
Brokers said the cut was still small and that the rates needed to go down further.

The Thai cabinet is expected to approve a total zero-coupon issue of 50 billion baht on Tuesday. The bonds are aimed at raising funds to help cash-strapped firms in the ailing property and financial sectors.
